c.tagline: Nepal's Terai gateway to Lumbini, birthplace of the Buddha.

taxi.fareNote: Taxis and auto-rickshaws are unmetered, so agree the fare before setting off; the Pathao and InDrive apps work in the Bhairahawa area and help fix a fair price.

emergency.note: 100 reaches the Nepal Police, 102 is the ambulance service, and 101 is the fire brigade; 1144 is a national tourist/traffic hotline.

avoid.reason: Watch for touts, rigged money-changers and overcharging rickshaws around the Sunauli/Belahiya India border crossing.

hood_desc: The busy commercial heart of Bhairahawa, packed with shops, hotels, money changers, and eateries; the practical base for travelers using the city as a launchpad to Lumbini and the Indian border.
A major crossroads and dining-and-shopping hub of the city, lively in the evenings with restaurants, sweet shops, and street food; good for travelers who want food and buzz near their hotel.
A central commercial junction lined with markets, textile and electronics shops, and local bazaars; suits shoppers and those wanting an everyday-Nepal Terai street scene.

The UNESCO-listed Sacred Garden 25 km west, where the Maya Devi Temple marks the Buddha's birthplace beside the Ashoka Pillar, sacred pond, and the international Monastic Zone of temples; the reason most visitors come, best for pilgrims and a peaceful overnight.
The border settlement 4 km south where Nepal meets Sunauli in India, a transit point of guesthouses, exchange counters, and bus stands; a functional, quieter base mainly for overland crossers.

water.note: Drink only bottled, boiled, or purified water throughout Nepal's Terai.

transit.hours: Auto-rickshaws, shared tempos, and buses run from early morning to mid-evening; after dark, private taxis and app rides are the main option.
transit.note: There is no metro or rail. Getting around is by auto-rickshaw, shared electric/diesel tempos, cycle-rickshaws, local buses, and taxis; Lumbini is reached by taxi, bus, or hired auto from the city.
transit.pay: Fares are paid in cash (Nepalese rupees) directly to the driver; shared tempos have fixed low fares while taxis and autos are negotiated. No transit card exists.

bus: Intercity buses to Kathmandu, Pokhara and Butwal
Local buses, shared tempos and auto-rickshaws to Lumbini and the border
train: No passenger rail in the city; the nearest Indian railhead is Nautanwa, across the border

airport.name: Gautam Buddha International Airport (BWA)
rentals: Local car and taxi hire operators

transit.m: Auto-rickshaw / shared tempo to the bazaar (10-15 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving about 10% at tourist restaurants and tipping guides and drivers is appreciated.

food.name: Dal bhat and Thakali thali
food.desc: The everyday Nepali plate: rice, lentil soup, seasonal vegetable curry, greens and pickle, refilled until you stop; Thakali sets add buckwheat and mutton.

places.name: Bhairahawa Cafe & Restro
places.note: Best-known cafe in town for Thakali sets and dal bhat, plus proper coffee.

places.name: New Dhaulagiri Restaurant
places.note: Family-run kitchen near the sacred garden doing honest Nepali plates.

places.name: Bama Tandoors
places.note: Popular local restaurant with both Nepali thali and North Indian dishes.

food.name: Momo
food.desc: Steamed or fried dumplings of buffalo, chicken or vegetables with a tomato-sesame achar dipping sauce; also served jhol style in a spiced broth.

places.name: Everest Momo and Restaurant
places.note: Simple, cheap and consistently praised for juicy, chilli-hot momos.

places.name: Bhairahawa Cafe & Restro
places.note: Reliable steamed and fried momos in an air-conditioned family setting.

places.name: Momo stalls around Milan Chowk
places.note: Evening street counters where locals eat momo by the plate for a few rupees.

food.name: Samosa, chaat and pani puri
food.desc: Terai street snacking shaped by the Indian border: fried potato samosas, spiced chickpea chaat, and puffed pani puri filled with tamarind water.

places.name: Street stalls at Buddha Chowk
places.note: The town's main junction; chaat and pani puri carts set up from late afternoon.

places.name: Bazaar stalls on Bank Road
places.note: Row of snack and sweet shops in the busiest shopping street.

places.name: BFC Foodland
places.note: Sit-down option for snacks, fried chicken and Indian-Chinese if the street is too busy.

food.name: Sel roti with aloo achar
food.desc: Ring-shaped rice-flour bread, crisp outside and soft inside, deep fried each morning and eaten with spicy potato pickle or plain yoghurt.

places.name: Morning stalls at Buddha Chowk
places.note: Fried fresh at dawn and sold by the ring; best in the first hour.

places.name: Sweet shops on Bank Road
places.note: Mithai shops stack sel roti beside jalebi and barfi, especially at festival time.

places.name: Bhairahawa Cafe & Restro
places.note: Occasionally serves it with the Nepali breakfast set if you miss the street sellers.

food.name: Lumbini vegetarian food
food.desc: Meat-free, often onion- and garlic-free cooking around the birthplace of the Buddha - vegetable curries, dal, rice and simple monastery-style meals.

places.name: Namaste Lumbini Tandoori Family Restaurant
places.note: Indian-Nepali kitchen at the sacred garden gate with a big vegetarian menu.

places.name: Monastic zone dining halls
places.note: Several international monasteries serve simple vegetarian meals to visiting pilgrims.

places.name: New Dhaulagiri Restaurant
places.note: Vegetable thali, parathas and rotis a short walk from the temple complex.

food.name: Tandoori roti and grills
food.desc: Clay-oven cooking straight over the border - butter naan, tandoori roti, marinated chicken tikka and paneer, eaten with thick gravies.

places.name: Bama Tandoors
places.note: Named for its tandoor; the local benchmark for breads and grilled meats.

places.name: Namaste Lumbini Tandoori Family Restaurant
places.note: Tandoori grills and curries, popular with pilgrims and guesthouse guests.

places.name: BFC Foodland
places.note: Busy all-rounder for tandoori plates, Indian and Chinese dishes.

food.name: Masala chai
food.desc: Strong milk tea boiled with ginger, cardamom and plenty of sugar, poured from stall to glass all day; the town's default social drink.

places.name: Tea stalls at Buddha Chowk
places.note: Glass-and-kettle stands at the main junction, busiest at dawn and dusk.

places.name: Bhairahawa Cafe & Restro
places.note: Sit-down chai plus espresso drinks if you want a break from the street.

places.name: Stalls at the Lumbini gate
places.note: Chai and biscuits for pilgrims outside the sacred garden entrance.

food.name: Lassi and sugarcane juice
food.desc: Sweet or salted curd lassi whisked to a froth, and fresh-pressed sugarcane juice with lime and black salt - Terai antidotes to the heat.

places.name: Sweet shops on Bank Road
places.note: Mithai shops serve thick lassi in steel tumblers alongside the sweets.

places.name: Juice carts at Buddha Chowk
places.note: Hand-cranked sugarcane presses at the junction, cheapest cold drink in town.

places.name: Namaste Lumbini Tandoori Family Restaurant
places.note: Lassi and fresh juices with the vegetarian thalis.

landmarks: Maya Devi Temple, Lumbini
The UNESCO-listed sacred birthplace of the Buddha, where a marker stone and ancient nativity sculpture pinpoint the exact spot of his birth.
Ashoka Pillar
The inscribed sandstone pillar erected by Emperor Ashoka in 249 BC, the earliest epigraphic proof that Lumbini is the Buddha's birthplace.
Puskarini Pond and Sacred Garden
The tranquil bathing pool where Queen Maya Devi is said to have bathed before giving birth, set among ancient stupa ruins and a great Bodhi tree.
World Peace Pagoda, Lumbini
A gleaming white Japanese-built stupa crowned in gold at the north end of Lumbini's ceremonial axis, radiating serenity across the wetlands.
Royal Thai Monastery
A stunning white-marble Thai temple with sweeping blue roofs, the most photographed monastery in Lumbini's international monastic zone.
Zhong Hua Chinese Monastery
A Forbidden City-style complex of pagoda roofs and courtyards where chanting monks welcome visitors in Lumbini's West Monastic Zone.
Myanmar Golden Temple
One of Lumbini's oldest monasteries, its gilded corncob-shaped shikhara echoing the great shrines of Bagan.
Lumbini Museum
A striking brick museum by architect Kenzo Tange's master plan, displaying artefacts, manuscripts and photographs tracing Buddhism's spread from Lumbini.
Tilaurakot (Kapilvastu)
Archaeological remains of the ancient Shakya capital where Prince Siddhartha spent his first 29 years, an evocative day trip west of Siddharthanagar.
Ramagrama Stupa
The only original, unopened relic stupa of the Buddha, a grassy sacred mound by the Jharahi River guarded, legend says, by nagas.

train.note: There is no railway in Siddharthanagar (Bhairahawa) or anywhere in western Nepal. The nearest railheads are across the border in India - Nautanwa, roughly 10 km beyond the Sunauli crossing, and the far better connected Gorakhpur junction about 95 km away, both on Indian Railways (https://www.irctc.co.in/). Trains from Nautanwa are infrequent, so most travellers take a taxi or shared jeep straight from Gorakhpur station to Sunauli, about two hours. Nepal's only cross-border train, the Jaynagar - Janakpur line, is far to the east and of no use here.

intl.to: Gorakhpur, Varanasi & Delhi (India) - Indian state and private buses from Sunauli, 4 km south of the town across the Belahiya border
intl.op: Sunauli bus stand operators — tickets at the Sunauli bus stand

bus.note: Siddharthanagar's own bus park handles Nepali services: Kathmandu is 7-10 hours via Butwal and Narayanghat, and Pokhara 5-6 hours either on the scenic but rough road through Tansen or the better route via Bharatpur; Lumbini is only 22 km away by local bus or taxi. For India you take a rickshaw or taxi the 4 km to Belahiya, walk across to Sunauli and pick up UP state or private buses to Gorakhpur (3 hours) and beyond - Delhi is a punishing 24-30 hours in total. The border is open around the clock but the Nepali and Indian immigration offices are set back from the road and must both be visited in person, and Sunauli has a long-standing reputation for touts and fake ticket agents, so buy at the official counters only.

ferry.note: Nepal is landlocked and there are no passenger boat services; the local rivers such as the Danda and Tinau are shallow, seasonal and unnavigable, so all travel here is by road or from Gautam Buddha International Airport just outside town.

full.name: Tansen
full.blurb: Hilltop Newari town on the Butwal-Pokhara highway with narrow winding lanes and old temples overlooking the Kaligandaki valley.

full.name: Chitwan National Park
full.blurb: UNESCO-listed lowland jungle park with rhino and tiger populations, reached by jeep safari through the Terai plains.

full.name: Shravasti
full.blurb: Ancient Buddhist pilgrimage town across the Indian border where the Buddha taught many of his sermons.
